newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai property agency seeks to float foreign bonds.
newsitem.headline: Thai property agency seeks to float foreign bonds.

text.p: State-run property support agency Property Loan Management Organisation (PLMO) said on Tuesday it will seek government permission to raise funds in foreign markets due to the tight domestic money supply.
"We are seeking to amend PLMO's regulations to allow it to issue bonds through securitisation in foreign markets," PLMO director Krairit Uchukanondchai told reporters.
"The move is to avoid competition for domestic funds with corporate and private sector under this tight liquidity situation," Krairit said.
PLMO has been assigned by the government to alleviate debt burdens of bank creditors and cash-strapped developers by refinancing selected real estate projects that face cash-flow problems.
PLMO late last month delayed planned auctions of up to 10 billion baht ($400 million), seven-year zero-coupon bonds due to tight money market liquidity.
The agency earlier on May 10 floated its first one billion baht, seven-year, zero-coupon bonds with an average 10.13 percent annual yield.
The government originally planned to authorise PLMO to float up to 100 billion baht bonds.
